Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; built on 3.2.0 PTR values Blizzard may revise. This is barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor rebuilt for the patch's least-discussed detail: while 3.2.0 cut Barbarian's offence hard, it quietly handed the class free defence. Raid Leader's Aspect now grants 7-10% Damage Reduction it never had, and Rage of Harrogath's cooldown reduction rate doubled from 1 second to 0.5. A class that lost 27% of its baseline damage scaling and gained mitigation should probably be played as a durable build rather than as a glass one, which is the opposite of what Season 14 Barbarian became. The variant swaps Upheaval for Hammer of the Ancients - the other core skill both PTR tier sources name alongside Ring of Red Furor - because its slower, heavier rhythm suits banking Fury better than Upheaval's, and it trades some clear speed for the ability to hold ground in Overland Ambushes and Challenge Dungeons, the two new PTR activities that punish squishy melee.

Rotation
  1. Keep War Cry, Challenging Shout and Rallying Cry rolling, bank Fury with Lunging Strike, then dump it into Hammer of the Ancients when the bar is high.
  2. Hold position inside the pack rather than cycling in and out - the damage reduction and Fortify are what pay for standing there.
Variants

Leveling — All three shouts up, Lunging Strike to fill the bar, Hammer of the Ancients when the bar is high. Build the Fury-banking habit from level one; it is unnatural for anyone who played Season 14 Whirlwind and it has to be learned deliberately.
Move on when Level 70 with Torment 1 unlocked and Ring of Red Furor in hand - the same gate as the base build, for the same reason.

Early Endgame — Three shouts maintained on rotation, Lunging Strike to bank Fury, Hammer of the Ancients in heavy dumps when the bar is high. Raid Leader's 7-10% Damage Reduction is now permanent rather than situational, so play forward into packs rather than kiting - that is the whole reason to run this variant instead of the base build.
Move on when Shout uptime near-continuous and resting Fury sitting well above 30. If shouts are dropping, add Cooldown Reduction before adding anything else.

Late Endgame — Shouts continuously, Lunging Strike to bank, Hammer of the Ancients in big dumps at high Fury. This variant holds position in packs rather than cycling in and out - Raid Leader's damage reduction, three-shout Fortify and the Armor weighting are all paying for the right to do that.
Move on when You can hold ground through a Challenge Dungeon two Torment tiers above your normal difficulty without dying. That is the specific capability this variant buys with its lost clear speed.

Pushing — The honest trade at push tiers: this variant clears slower than barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor and dies less. In the Pit, where clear time is the score, that is usually the wrong trade and you should push the base build. In Challenge Dungeons scaled three Torment tiers up, in Overland Ambushes, and in Hardcore, it is the right one. It also inherits the base build's central risk unchanged: everything rests on Ring of Red Furor surviving to launch in its current form, and a 1%[x] per-Fury bonus with no stated cap is exactly the kind of line that gets tuned. All values are 3.2.0 PTR values.

PTR status: same as the base build - reused from the verified Season 14 Barbarian entries, diablo4lootfilter.com/filters confirmed reachable 2026-08-08 (diablofilter.com/browse: HTTP 403 twice, unreachable). No Season 15 filter exists. Search class Barbarian, endgame strictness, then loosen it deliberately: this variant values Maximum Life and Armor rolls that a damage-focused Barbarian code will hide, and it needs rings kept for Ring of Red Furor and jewelry kept for Soul Splinter sockets.

Uniques
  • ring PTR route: PTR Boosts from the vendor Mrak next to the main Waypoint in any major city. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0; exists in Season 14's general unique pool, so expect a lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe. Mandatory here as in the base build - the Fury-banking plan has no payoff without it. Where →
  • helm PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged by 3.2.0): general unique pool - lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on a Common helm. Where →
  • pants PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged by 3.2.0): Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on Common pants (1 Enhanced Primordial Dust and 10 Primordial Dust), not a dedicated boss. Where →
  • amulet Iconic Mythic. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route on 3.2.0: the Jeweler's rune craft with slot selection (no Crafted tag, so it does not spend your one crafted-Mythic slot), a Blacksmith Mythic cache which now drops Iconic Mythics without the Crafted-tag restriction, or the Horadric Cube's 1:1 upgrade if you are willing to spend the Crafted slot. Season 14's gearing rule still binds and is not optional: it doubles your resource pool and turns it into an effective life pool, so it wants zero Life on gear - which directly contradicts this variant's Maximum Life priorities. Run it or run Life rolls, not both. Where →
  • weapon Iconic Mythic. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route on 3.2.0: Jeweler rune craft with slot selection (no Crafted tag), Blacksmith Mythic cache, or the Horadric Cube 1:1 upgrade. Prefer the Jeweler or Blacksmith route to keep the Crafted slot free. Where →
  • SSplinter of Anguish jewelry socket New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. Default pick - its 15-35% Critical Strike Chance compounds with Ring of Red Furor's Bonus Critical Strike Damage. Splinter of Hellfire remains disqualified (-100% Critical Strike Chance). Where →
  • SSplinter of Pain jewelry socket New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. The alternative pick that only this variant can justify: 10-40% Damage Reduction for -30% Movement Speed. A deliberately durable melee build that plans to hold ground can pay a movement-speed cost the base build cannot. Test it head to head against Anguish in Challenge Dungeons before deciding - the honest expectation is that Anguish wins on damage and Pain wins on deaths, and which matters depends on the content. Where →
  • Target-farm Grigoire, The Galvanic Saint, an Initiate-tier Lair boss (1x Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • Target-farm The Butcher, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • ring Mythic Unique with no dedicated boss: every Lair boss can drop it, or craft it in the Horadric Cube with Pandemonium Fragments - remembering that only one Cube-crafted Mythic may be equipped at a time. Where →

Point allocation, in order66 points across 10 nodes

[ptr] Provenance, stated plainly. No 3.2.0 skill tree is published for any build on any site - the official notes carry no allocations, and Maxroll, Icy Veins, d4builds and d4guides were all still serving Season 14 guides on 2026-08-08, day 5 of the 8-day PTR. This allocation is therefore the specialist's, built from the skill list the PTR digest authorises for this class plus the 3.2.0 changes that actually apply. Treat the point counts as a starting shape to test, not as a published build. Where a skill's upgrade mods are named below, those names are carried over from Season 14 planner data - 3.2.0 does not rename them. Where a skill appears with no mods, that is deliberate: its mod names were not published anywhere consulted, and inventing them would be worse than leaving them out. On the PTR you can skip this stage outright - Mrak's boosts grant level 70 and maxed aspects directly - so this allocation is written for what a live Season 15 would look like. This variant runs Rallying Cry from level one where the Upheaval build runs Leap - the durability thesis starts at the levelling bar, not at endgame.

Skill point priority

  1. Hammer of the Ancients to max - the core skill this variant banks Fury for
  2. Lunging Strike for Fury generation, still capped at 0.5 Fury per 1% Maximum Life since 3.1.x
  3. All three shouts taken early rather than late: this variant is built on shout uptime for Berserking, Vulnerable, Fortify and damage reduction together
  4. Wrath of the Berserker as the ultimate for its flat +30% all damage
  5. Skip Leap - the sixth slot goes to the third shout instead, which is the first visible divergence from the base build

Board & glyph focus

Maximum Fury maxed, survivability second, Critical Strike Damage third. The Melted Heart of Selig decision lands here and it is a genuine fork, not a default: it doubles the Fury pool - which under Ring of Red Furor means doubling the damage multiplier - but it wants zero Life on gear, which contradicts every Maximum Life priority listed above. Either commit to Selig and strip Life rolls in favour of Armor and damage reduction, or skip Selig and keep the Life-based durability. Do not half-do it. Also carried from the base build: do not equip Ramaladni's Magnum Opus, whose PTR drain of 10% of Maximum Fury scales up as your pool grows and fights the entire plan.

How to run them

[ptr] 3.2.0 changes nothing about mercenaries - the words "Mercenary" and "Mercenaries" and all four mercenary names are absent from the official 3.2.0 notes entirely. So this is the Season 14 pairing carried over, which is the only guidance that exists. Hire Raheir for Valiance's rotating cheat-death and Inspiration's damage multiplier, and reinforce with Aldkin on Field of Languish for area damage reduction - this is the durability variant, so it takes the defensive branch of the Season 14 either/or rather than the offensive one. One PTR-specific point worth making: Barbarian's core stat scalar was cut 1.1 to 0.8, so the class is measurably squishier per point of Strength than it was in Season 14 - if you find yourself dying on the PTR where you did not before, swapping Varyana for Aldkin's Field of Languish is the honest response, and it is a pairing Maxroll already endorses for Barbarian.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; built on 3.2.0 PTR values Blizzard may revise. This is barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor rebuilt for the patch's least-discussed detail: while 3.2.0 cut Barbarian's offence hard, it quietly handed the class free defence. Raid Leader's Aspect now grants 7-10% Damage Reduction it never had, and Rage of Harrogath's cooldown reduction rate doubled from 1 second to 0.5. A class that lost 27% of its baseline damage scaling and gained mitigation should probably be played as a durable build rather than as a glass one, which is the opposite of what Season 14 Barbarian became. The variant swaps Upheaval for Hammer of the Ancients - the other core skill both PTR tier sources name alongside Ring of Red Furor - because its slower, heavier rhythm suits banking Fury better than Upheaval's, and it trades some clear speed for the ability to hold ground in Overland Ambushes and Challenge Dungeons, the two new PTR activities that punish squishy melee.

Rotation
  1. Keep War Cry, Challenging Shout and Rallying Cry rolling, bank Fury with Lunging Strike, then dump it into Hammer of the Ancients when the bar is high.
  2. Hold position inside the pack rather than cycling in and out - the damage reduction and Fortify are what pay for standing there.
Variants

Leveling — All three shouts up, Lunging Strike to fill the bar, Hammer of the Ancients when the bar is high. Build the Fury-banking habit from level one; it is unnatural for anyone who played Season 14 Whirlwind and it has to be learned deliberately.
Move on when Level 70 with Torment 1 unlocked and Ring of Red Furor in hand - the same gate as the base build, for the same reason.

Early Endgame — Three shouts maintained on rotation, Lunging Strike to bank Fury, Hammer of the Ancients in heavy dumps when the bar is high. Raid Leader's 7-10% Damage Reduction is now permanent rather than situational, so play forward into packs rather than kiting - that is the whole reason to run this variant instead of the base build.
Move on when Shout uptime near-continuous and resting Fury sitting well above 30. If shouts are dropping, add Cooldown Reduction before adding anything else.

Late Endgame — Shouts continuously, Lunging Strike to bank, Hammer of the Ancients in big dumps at high Fury. This variant holds position in packs rather than cycling in and out - Raid Leader's damage reduction, three-shout Fortify and the Armor weighting are all paying for the right to do that.
Move on when You can hold ground through a Challenge Dungeon two Torment tiers above your normal difficulty without dying. That is the specific capability this variant buys with its lost clear speed.

Pushing — The honest trade at push tiers: this variant clears slower than barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor and dies less. In the Pit, where clear time is the score, that is usually the wrong trade and you should push the base build. In Challenge Dungeons scaled three Torment tiers up, in Overland Ambushes, and in Hardcore, it is the right one. It also inherits the base build's central risk unchanged: everything rests on Ring of Red Furor surviving to launch in its current form, and a 1%[x] per-Fury bonus with no stated cap is exactly the kind of line that gets tuned. All values are 3.2.0 PTR values.

Uniques
  • ring PTR route: PTR Boosts from the vendor Mrak next to the main Waypoint in any major city. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0; exists in Season 14's general unique pool, so expect a lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe. Mandatory here as in the base build - the Fury-banking plan has no payoff without it. Where →
  • helm PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged by 3.2.0): general unique pool - lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on a Common helm. Where →
  • pants PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged by 3.2.0): Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on Common pants (1 Enhanced Primordial Dust and 10 Primordial Dust), not a dedicated boss. Where →
  • amulet Iconic Mythic. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route on 3.2.0: the Jeweler's rune craft with slot selection (no Crafted tag, so it does not spend your one crafted-Mythic slot), a Blacksmith Mythic cache which now drops Iconic Mythics without the Crafted-tag restriction, or the Horadric Cube's 1:1 upgrade if you are willing to spend the Crafted slot. Season 14's gearing rule still binds and is not optional: it doubles your resource pool and turns it into an effective life pool, so it wants zero Life on gear - which directly contradicts this variant's Maximum Life priorities. Run it or run Life rolls, not both. Where →
  • weapon Iconic Mythic. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route on 3.2.0: Jeweler rune craft with slot selection (no Crafted tag), Blacksmith Mythic cache, or the Horadric Cube 1:1 upgrade. Prefer the Jeweler or Blacksmith route to keep the Crafted slot free. Where →
  • SSplinter of Anguish jewelry socket New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. Default pick - its 15-35% Critical Strike Chance compounds with Ring of Red Furor's Bonus Critical Strike Damage. Splinter of Hellfire remains disqualified (-100% Critical Strike Chance). Where →
  • SSplinter of Pain jewelry socket New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. The alternative pick that only this variant can justify: 10-40% Damage Reduction for -30% Movement Speed. A deliberately durable melee build that plans to hold ground can pay a movement-speed cost the base build cannot. Test it head to head against Anguish in Challenge Dungeons before deciding - the honest expectation is that Anguish wins on damage and Pain wins on deaths, and which matters depends on the content. Where →
  • Target-farm Grigoire, The Galvanic Saint, an Initiate-tier Lair boss (1x Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • Target-farm The Butcher, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →
  • ring Mythic Unique with no dedicated boss: every Lair boss can drop it, or craft it in the Horadric Cube with Pandemonium Fragments - remembering that only one Cube-crafted Mythic may be equipped at a time. Where →

Reasoning

Based onRing of Red Furor Upheaval Barbarian
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. Core skill swap: Upheaval out, Hammer of the Ancients in. Both are named by both PTR tier sources as Ring of Red Furor cores. Hammer of the Ancients' slower cadence means fewer, larger Fury dumps, which keeps the bar higher on average - and bar height is literally the multiplier under Ring of Red Furor's 1%[x] Bonus Critical Strike Damage per Fury above 30.
  2. Rallying Cry promoted from filler to permanent. Its Madawc damage variant was halved on the PTR so it is no longer a damage skill, but its Fortify and Unstoppable are worth more now, and Rage of Harrogath's doubled cooldown-reduction rate makes keeping it up cheaper than it was in Season 14.
  3. Aspect swap: Aspect of Elemental Fate out, Raid Leader's Aspect promoted to a permanent slot at every stage. Its new 7-10% Damage Reduction is a straight PTR gift and the meta build only picks it up at some stages.
  4. Aspect swap: Aspect of Crushing out, Aspect of Heavenly Strength in at late stages, keeping the two-hander defensive enabler on rather than dropping it for a damage aspect once gear improves.
  5. Paragon reweighting: Maximum Fury first as in the base build - that is non-negotiable, it is the multiplier - but survivability nodes take priority over the second tier of damage nodes rather than the reverse.
  6. Gear reweighting: Maximum Life and Armor rolls are taken over the third damage affix on every slot. The base build takes damage there.
  7. Soul Splinter: still Splinter of Anguish over Splinter of Hellfire, for the same reason as the base build - Ring of Red Furor pays out in Bonus Critical Strike Damage and Hellfire's -100% Critical Strike Chance would mean never collecting it. Splinter of Pain is the one genuine alternative here and only here: 10-40% Damage Reduction for -30% Movement Speed is a trade a deliberately durable melee build can actually make, where the base build cannot. Test both.
  8. This variant is not faster. If you want clear speed, play the base build; this one exists to survive content that kills the base build.

Endurant Faith

Unique Charm

  • When you would be damaged for at least 30% of your Maximum Life at once, it is instead distributed over the next 4 seconds and reduced by 15 – 20%.

Despite the Light's blessings, countless Knights Penitent were hewn apart by the infernal hordes. Remnants of their steel lie scattered through the Hells – dwindling lights in the chaos.

BasicMobilityMartial

Rank 5/15

Generate Fury: 12

Lucky Hit Chance: 50%

Lunge forward and strike an enemy, dealing 90% damage.

Modifiers

  • LSkewerLunging Strike deals 75%[x] increased damage and an additional 5%[x] increased damage for each target you lunge through, up to 100%[x].
  • BerserkingLunging Strike grants Berserking for 3 seconds when it Critically Strikes. Lunging Strike gains 5%[+] increased Critical Strike Chance.

War Cry

BrawlingShoutCombat

Rank 15/15

Cooldown: 25 seconds

Bellow a mighty war cry, increasing your damage dealt by 7.5% for 4.0 seconds.

Nearby allies gain half of War Cry's effects.

Modifiers

  • Mighty RoarWar Cry's damage bonus is increased by 10% and allies now receive its full effect. You also gain Berserking for 4 seconds.
  • FerocityWar Cry grants 2 stacks of Ferocity.
  • VulnerableWar Cry makes nearby enemies Vulnerable for 4 seconds.

Challenging Shout

DefensiveShoutCombat

Rank 15/15

Cooldown: 25 seconds

Taunt Nearby enemies and gain 20.0% Damage Reduction for 8.0 seconds.

Modifiers

  • RagingChallenging Shout causes enemies to burn with rage, dealing 600% Burning damage over 8 seconds. You no longer gain Damage Reduction from Challenging Shout but instead gain 20%[x] increased damage against Burning enemies.
  • Damage BonusThe first 5 enemies Taunted by Challenging Shout take 20%[x] increased damage from you.
  • WeakenChallenging Shout Weakens enemies.
